articles.title: Lionel Messi retires from Argentina national team after six World Cup appearances
articles.summary:
Lionel Messi has played his last game representing Argentina, the soccer star announced Monday. 
The 39-year-old Messi’s retirement from the national team comes 20 years after his first appearance and ends a career with La Albiceleste that saw him score 98 goals and add 38 assists in 142 matches.
articles.body: Lionel Messi has played his last game representing Argentina, the soccer star announced Monday. The 39-year-old Messi’s retirement from the national team comes 20 years after his first appearance and ends a career with La Albiceleste that saw him score 125 goals and add 68 assists in 207 matches. Messi played in six World Cups, winning in 2022 and playing in the 2014 and 2026 finals. He became the all-time leading scorer in World Cup history during the tournament this summer with 21 goals, only for France’s Kylian Mbappé to overtake him with 22 goals. “I leave with the peace of mind and pride of having given you —together with my teammates — moments we’d only dreamed of,” Messi wrote on social media, in a translation from Spanish. “It was incredible to have lived through it all with you.” Messi posted that he wrote the announcement of his retirement two days after Argentina’s loss to Spain in July’s World Cup final, and after a pause that included mourning the death of his father, “I’m more convinced than ever” it was time to take off Argentina’s famed blue-and-white-striped kit. “It was a decision that hurt — and still hurts — deep in the soul, but I understand that it’s time,” Messi wrote. “I swear to you that I always gave it my all — not just in recent years, but even before we won everything — and I always fought hard and gave everything I had for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you proud to be Argentine through soccer.” “There’s not much time left, and chapters are coming to a close —and this is one that hurts me deeply. I love, have loved, and will always love being on the national team. I’ve given it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are some truly great young players coming up who deserve their spot,” he wrote. “Thank you for all the love over these 20 years. I’m going to miss hearing from you all so much from the sidelines. Now I’ll be just one of you, always cheering and supporting from the sidelines (through the good times and the bad — especially the bad),” he said. Messi continues to play professionally for the MLS club Inter Miami. While playing for the giant Spanish club Barcelona, Messi quickly found success and rose to prominence as a transcendent talent in the early 2010s. His path with his national team was rockier, however. Messi was best known for leading Argentina to major finals such as the Copa América, the storied tournament between South American nations, and the 2014 World Cup, only to lose. After his third Copa América final defeat in 2016, a loss that included a penalty miss by Messi in a shootout, Messi said, “For me, the national team is over. I’ve done all I can. It hurts not to be a champion. … It was the thing I wanted the most but I couldn’t get it, so I think it’s over. I think this is best for everyone.” Only weeks later, Messi reversed course and recommitted to playing for his nation. “I see there are many problems in Argentinian football and I don’t intend to create another one,” he said in 2016. “I don’t want to cause any damage, I’ve always tried to do just the opposite, to help all that I can.” “We need to fix many things in Argentinian football, but I prefer to do this from inside and not criticize from outside,” he said. Messi’s inability to lead Argentina to titles early in his career even earned criticism from Diego Maradona, the Argentine legend who led the country to the World Cup title in 1986 and later coached Messi with the national team. Both wore the No. 10 jersey, and Messi was constantly compared to Maradona. “We shouldn’t deify Messi any longer,” Maradona said in an interview with Fox Sports. “He’s Messi when he plays for Barcelona. Messi is Messi when he wears that shirt and he’s another Messi with Argentina.” The national team’s fortunes did not change overnight with Messi’s return in 2016, including an exit in the round of 16 in 2018 and a third-place finish in the 2019 Copa América. Once international soccer resumed following Covid-related delays, however, Argentina and Messi won the 2021 Copa América and the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and repeated as Copa champion in 2024. His World Cup performance this summer showed that Messi’s gifts for scoring had not been degraded by age. His eight goals were second only to Mbappé for the tournament, and Messi added four assists, as well.

articles.title: Lionel Messi’s 10 most iconic moments as Argentina legend retires from international football
articles.summary: Football News: Lionel Messi has finally closed the book on his extraordinary Argentina career.At 39, after nearly two decades wearing the famous blue-and-white shirt.
articles.body: Lionel Messi has finally closed the book on his extraordinary Argentina career.At 39, after nearly two decades wearing the famous blue-and-white shirt, Messi has announced his retirement from international football, ending a journey that took him from a teenage debutant in 2005 to Argentina captain and World Cup-winning legend. He leaves after six World Cups, two Copa America titles and the greatest prize of all — the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. He also led Argentina to the 2026 World Cup final, where they lost to Spain.Messi's international career was not always the fairytale it became. There were lost finals, criticism and even a brief retirement from international football in 2016. But the final chapter transformed his legacy, with Argentina winning the Copa America in 2021, the 2022 World Cup and another Copa America in 2024. His decision to walk away now brings an emotional end to one of football's greatest international careers.Messi said the decision was painful but that he understood the time had come. He revealed that he had written his retirement statement on July 21, two days after Argentina's 2026 World Cup final defeat to Spain, but waited before publishing it as his father was facing serious health issues.From his first World Cup goal to his long-awaited international triumph, here are 10 moments that defined Messi's remarkable journey.1. World Cup debut and first goal — 2006Messi announced himself on football's biggest stage as an 18-year-old at the 2006 World Cup in Germany. Against Serbia and Montenegro, he came off the bench, assisted Hernán Crespo and then scored in a 6-0 victory. He became Argentina's youngest World Cup player and scorer at the time.2. Meeting Diego Maradona — 2010The 2010 World Cup brought Messi together with another Argentine icon, Diego Maradona, who was then the national team's coach. Messi arrived in South Africa as one of the world's biggest stars after establishing himself at Barcelona, but Argentina's campaign ended in a heavy quarter-final defeat to Germany. The tournament nonetheless marked an important stage in Messi's evolution as the face of Argentine football.3. Breaking Barcelona’s scoring record — 2012Messi surpassed César Rodríguez to become Barcelona's all-time leading scorer with a hat-trick against Granada on March 20, 2012. He equalled the 232-goal mark with his first goal, broke it with his second and extended it with his third. He eventually left Barcelona with 672 goals, a record that underlined his extraordinary impact at the club.4. The 91-goal year — 2012Messi produced one of the most astonishing scoring years football has ever seen in 2012. He finished with 91 goals for Barcelona and Argentina, including 79 for his club and 12 for his country. The remarkable tally surpassed Gerd Müller’s previous calendar-year record and earned Messi his fourth consecutive Ballon d'Or.5. Breaking La Liga’s scoring record — 2014Another hat-trick delivered another historic record. Messi scored three times against Sevilla in November 2014 to surpass Telmo Zarra as La Liga's all-time leading scorer. Zarra's 251-goal record had stood since 1955. Messi eventually finished his La Liga career with 474 goals, still comfortably ahead of Cristiano Ronaldo's 311 for Real Madrid.6. First senior international trophy — 2021For years, the biggest criticism of Messi's Argentina career was his failure to win a senior international trophy. That finally changed at the Maracana in July 2021. Argentina beat Brazil 1-0 in the Copa America final, with Ángel Di María scoring the decisive goal. Messi, who had scored four goals during the tournament, was named its best player. The emotional images of Messi collapsing to the ground at the final whistle and being lifted by his teammates became symbolic of years of frustration finally being released.7. World Cup glory in Qatar — 2022This was the moment that completed Messi's collection. Argentina beat France on penalties after a breathtaking 3-3 draw in the 2022 World Cup final. Messi scored twice, converted Argentina's first penalty in the shootout and was named the tournament's best player after scoring seven goals. He became the first player to score in every round of the tournament, while Argentina ended a 36-year wait for the World Cup.8. Eighth Ballon d'Or — 2023The World Cup triumph also delivered another individual landmark. Messi won the Ballon d'Or for a record eighth time in 2023, with his victory largely driven by his performances in Qatar. It was another reminder that his international success had finally caught up with the individual brilliance he had displayed throughout his career.9. World Cup’s top scorer (briefly)The Argentina captain produced another remarkable campaign at 2026 FIFA World Cup, scoring eight goals to take his World Cup tally to 21 — briefly making him the tournament’s all-time leading scorer. Kylian Mbappé subsequently moved past him to 22 goals in the third-place match against England.10. His final World Cup — 2026Messi's final World Cup provided one last chapter to his extraordinary Argentina story. At 39, he led Argentina all the way to the final, where they suffered a 0-1 extra-time defeat to Spain. But his individual campaign provided another memorable chapter on football’s biggest stage.Two days after that final, Messi had already made his decision.For Argentina, there will never be another Messi. For nearly 20 years, he carried the weight of a football-mad nation, endured the disappointment of lost finals and eventually delivered the trophies his country had craved.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jan Lagunas está a punto de salir
articles.standfirst: Será cedido a un conjunto puntero de la Primera división de Andorra: la llegada de Owono le sacó de la terna de porteros en la que aparecía como tercer figurante
articles.summary: Será cedido a un conjunto puntero de la Primera división de Andorra: la llegada de Owono le sacó de la terna de porteros en la que aparecía como tercer figurante
articles.body: Hace tan solo dos semanas se anunció que Jan Lagunas, Stefan Golubović y Tiago Olmedo, del Gimnàstic de Manresa, formarían parte del primer equipo del Andorra pese a mantener ficha de filial. En este sentido, en el caso del primero, el club apuntó que se contaba con él para completar la terna de porteros como tercer figurante, pero la reciente llegada de Jesús Owono ha obligado a buscarle destino. Es en este punto, el Periòdic d'Andorra avanza que ha entrado en juego la Lliga Multisegur Assegurances, la Primera división nacional de Andorra. De hecho, ha sido la misma dirección deportiva tricolor la que ha ofrecido el guardameta a uno de los conjuntos punteros de la categoría para que sume minutos de calidad en una liga mucho más competitiva que la Primera Catalana en la que compite el filial pirenaico. Se trataría, dejando de lado al Inter de Escaldes, de uno de los dos equipos que han jugado este año ronda previa europea: el FC Santa Coloma o el Atlètic d'Escaldes. Cabe mencionar que Lagunas, de solo 19 años, ha sido suplente con el Andorra en las dos primeras jornadas ligueras, pero ayer, contra el Eibar, su puesto ya lo ocupó Owono. La pasada temporada también fue convocado en los tres partidos que coincidieron con las ventanas de selecciones: la visita a Ipurúa contra el Eibar, en Zubieta contra la Real Sociedad B y en El Plantío ante el Burgos.

articles.title: David Soria ya es historia de LaLiga: el jugador con más titularidades consecutivas
articles.standfirst: El guardameta azulón suma 193 encuentros seguidos saliendo desde el inicio
articles.summary: El guardameta azulón suma 193 encuentros seguidos saliendo desde el inicio
articles.body: David Soria vuelve a ser titular con el Getafe. El guardameta azulón hace historia este lunes en el encuentro frente a Osasuna al lograr su titularidad 193 consecutiva, superando a Larrañaga, al que empató la semana pasada en el encuentro frente al Real Racing Club de Santander. Con ello, el meta madrileño se coloca en solitario, con todas las papeletas de seguir aumentando esos registros al ser clave en el esquema del Getafe de José Bordalás. La última suplencia de David Soria en LaLiga fue en la última jornada de la temporada 20/21. Desde entonces, el jugador, que arrancó la 21/22 defendiendo la meta desde el inicio frente al Valencia, allá por agosto de 2021, no ha dejado de guardar el arco azulón en competición liguera, siendo, durante ya cinco años consecutivos, amo y señor de la portería del sur de la Comunidad de Madrid. Soria suma, más allá de esos datos de titularidades consecutivas, 305 encuentros -contando el de hoy en El Sadar-, defendiendo la casaca azulona entre Liga, Copa del Rey, Europa League y Conference League, siendo de los pocos jugadores en la historia del club con dos participaciones en competición europea. En su novena temporada en el club, Soria ya se coloca como el cuarto jugador en la historia con más encuentros. Superó la pasada campaña a Damián, con 295, y busca ahora batir a Angelín, que sumó 319. Si sigue la trayectoria, y todo apunta que seguirá, el guardameta podría acabar la temporada superando al, actualmente, jugador con más partidos, Caballero, que suma 335, al igual que Djené, que con 327 es el segundo futbolista azulón con más apariciones con 328.

articles.title: Cody Gakpo transfer news: Man City's proposed £80m move for Liverpool forward close to collapse
articles.summary: Manchester City's proposed £80m move for Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo is close to collapsing.
articles.body:
Manchester City 's proposed £80m move for Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo is close to collapsing.

City had opened talks with Liverpool over a deal for the Netherlands international, with the Reds willing to sell Gakpo provided they could sign a replacement.

Liverpool completed the signing of France forward Bradley Barcola from Paris St-Germain for a fee worth up to £123m on Monday but would want another attacking player if Gakpo were to leave.

The Anfield club had targeted moves for Brighton 's Yankuba Minteh and Crystal Palace 's Ismaila Sarr but the valuation of both players has proved problematic.

Liverpool are now expected to keep Gakpo, 27, unless they are able to revive a deal for a new winger before Tuesday's deadline.

City agreed a £65m deal with Everton for winger Iliman Ndiaye on Monday .

Ndiaye, 26, was expected to join Tottenham , but the Senegal international is now set to be Enzo Maresca's latest signing..

articles.title: La UD recurre la roja de Jesé en Montilivi
articles.standfirst: Las Palmas, que juega el viernes ante el Leganés, conocerá la resolución el miércoles
articles.summary: La UD, que juega el viernes, conocerá la resolución el miércoles
articles.body: Las Palmas no se resigna a perder a Jesé para el duelo del viernes en el Gran Canaria ante el Leganés. El conjunto amarillo ha presentado un recurso contra la expulsión del delantero en Montilivi, donde vio la roja directa tras una acción con Izan. Jesé mostró su disconformidad con la decisión y así se lo hizo saber al colegiado Fuentes Molina, que reflejó en el acta que el futbolista fue expulsado “por dar una patada a un contrario, haciendo uso de fuerza excesiva, sin estar el balón a distancia de ser jugado”. El club grancanario entiende que la acción no era merecedora de la expulsión y confía en que el recurso prospere para poder recuperar a una de sus principales referencias ofensivas. De salir favorable, Jesé estaría disponible para medirse al Leganés de Morata este viernes en el Gran Canaria, en un duelo que añadiría un aliciente especial a la cita. El delantero amarillo espera ahora la resolución mientras mantiene la esperanza de poder estar a disposición de Rubén de la Barrera. La decisión no se conocerá hasta el miércoles, por lo que el técnico tendrá que preparar el encuentro con esa duda. De la Barrera deberá trabajar sobre los dos escenarios posibles: planificar con el atacante en sus planes o buscar una alternativa si la sanción se mantiene. Iván Jaime dejó buenas sensaciones y su posible titular en banda haría que Jefté jugase como delantero centro.

articles.title: Lionel Messi retires: How Argentina legend's decade of dominance almost never happened
articles.summary: Lionel Messi's decade of dominance with Argentina that almost never happened will go down as one of football's greatest ever stories.
articles.body:
"I've given it my all, I have nothing left to give."

Lionel Messi retired from international football on Monday as Argentina's all-time leading scorer and most-capped player. He captained them to World Cup glory at Qatar 2022 and to Copa America triumphs in 2021 and 2024.

But the world was almost denied his most successful period in the famous blue and white shirt.

On Sunday, 26 June 2016, at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, Messi broke the hearts of a nation.

Just two days after his 29th birthday and soon after missing a penalty in Argentina's Copa America final loss to Chile in a shootout, Messi decided he had seen enough.

After 113 appearances, he was adamant. In his mind, he would never pull on an Argentina shirt again.

"For me, the national team is over. I've done all I can. It hurts not to be a champion," he said.

The pain was understandable. Argentina had lost in the 2014 World Cup final, plus Copa America finals in 2007, 2015 and now 2016. The player many classed as the world's greatest had failed when it mattered most for him.

"It was the thing I wanted the most, but I couldn't get it, so I think it's over," Messi said, fighting back tears after another trophy chance slipped away. "I think this is best for everyone."

Fortunately for Argentina, Messi would have second thoughts.

Over the subsequent 10 years, he completed one of football's greatest ever stories. But it was a decade of dominance that almost never happened.

Since that retirement U-turn, Messi has played a further 94 times and scored another 70 goals for Argentina. He has lifted four major trophies.

The six-week period between his June 2016 retirement declaration and the 12 August announcement he would play on for the "love of the country" could be considered the most significant in Argentine football history - even in world football.

Messi retires from Argentina duty with 'nothing left to give'

Goals, records, tears ... Messi's most iconic moments

As Messi departs the international stage, words of criticism 10 years ago from the country's other legendary number 10 seem almost laughable.

"He's a really good person, but he has no personality," Diego Maradona said just weeks before Messi's first retirement. "He lacks the character to be a leader."

Back then it was the comparison with Maradona that was held against him. Yet Messi had already won eight La Liga titles and four Champions Leagues with Barcelona and was a five-time Ballon d'Or winner, and not yet 30.

Maradona's club career hadn't come close, but Messi's only major international honour had been Olympic gold at the 2008 Games. Maradona had almost single-handedly won the 1986 World Cup for Argentina.

It's hard to imagine it now, with Messi shirts dominating the last two World Cups, the Argentina team being built completely around him and the nation's fans worshipping him to an almost religious extent – but, back then, there was a lot of criticism.

"He's not as good as Diego", "he goes missing on the big occasion", "he is part of the country's failure". All accusations that were thrown in his direction.

This wasn't the first time Messi had considered walking away either.

Spanish football expert – and Messi biographer – Guillem Balague said: "Leo goes really down when he loses. He felt the pressure of being the captain of Argentina and the Maradona thing.

"Pecho Frio, people in Argentina called him, which means cold chest. It was an insult to say he had milk in his veins. So when he failed in 2016 at the Copa America, that was the third time – the first time in public – he had decided to leave the national side.

"The two previous ones was a matter of letting him lick his wounds, but this one he came out and said I've had enough. He sometimes cannot help himself as he says what he thinks."

The Maradona versus Messi debate is now surely over. Messi is Argentina's greatest, by most judgements. There are many who will say he is challenging Pele for the title of football's greatest ever.

Even people who criticised Messi eventually said sorry.

From the moment Messi quit his country, shockwaves reverberated around Argentina.

Yes, he had lost in four successive finals. But he was also the country's record goalscorer and the world's best player.

The 'Get Messi back' campaign started immediately as team-mates called for him to change his mind just minutes after his announcement.

"I can't imagine a national team without Messi," said goalkeeper Sergio Romero.

The social hashtag #NoTeVayasMessi (Don't go Messi) was used more than 20,000 times within 24 hours.

By that time, Argentina's President Mauricio Macri had already spoken with Messi over the phone to try to convince the Barcelona star to reconsider.

"I told him not to pay any attention to the comments being made because, in truth, we are very happy" with the job he has done," Macri told journalists at the time.

Less than a day later, the mayor of Buenos Aires, Horacio Rodriguez Larreta, had unveiled a statue in Messi's honour and called on the public to show him their love.

"As a football fan, Leo, I am asking you to please reconsider your decision," the mayor said.

Thousands of fans gathered in central Buenos Aires, while street signs throughout the capital displayed implored Messi to play on for Argentina.

Maradona stated Messi had to stay to take the team to the 2018 World Cup.

Edgardo Bauza became Argentina coach in August 2016, replacing Gerardo Martino after the Copa America failure. He lasted just eight months – but maybe his first few days were his most important.

The first thing he did was travel to Barcelona to persuade Messi to change his mind. The huge clamour for Messi to return proved irresistible.

"I love this country and this shirt too much," Messi said as he returned to the international fold.

"I'm grateful to all the people who wanted me to continue playing with Argentina. Hopefully we can give them something to cheer about soon."

Still, success didn't come instantly. In 2018, Argentina fell to France in the last 16 of the World Cup and many wrote off Messi's chances of ever lifting the trophy.

Quite incredibly, Messi did not win a senior international tournament until the age of 34 - and then he went on to win four in barely three years, including the 2022 Finalissima.

Questions about his international future were raised after each of those triumphs, but he played on to his sixth World Cup in 2026 where he scored eight goals and registered four assists en route to Argentina's defeat by Spain in the final.

He was strolling through games, lacking the speed of years gone by, but somehow proving every bit as effective.

The final took place in the same stadium where Messi 'retired' a decade earlier.

"When Messi retired [10 years ago] it reminded us all how much we loved him," said Argentina fan Benjamin who was in the Metlife for the 2016 showpiece final.

"When I heard him retire, I cried, the country cried. He did get criticism but only because everyone cared so much. Without Lionel Messi, Argentina would still be waiting for their next World Cup since 1986."

Messi's footballing future became a matter of fresh doubt after the death of his father Jorge just three weeks after this year's World Cup final.

This decision seems final and, at 39, another return to international football looks unlikely.

But South American football writer Tim Vickery said an official farewell in Argentina could be on the cards.

"Remember that, as a result of their behaviour at the World Cup, the next game Argentina play on home soil will only be in front of a crowd at 50% capacity," Vickery told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"But once those punishments are out of the way, I'm sure it will be in the mind of the Argentina FA: 'Why don't we hold a game back in Buenos Aires? River Plate, they have the biggest capacity in South America. Why don't we do an official farewell there? What do you think about it, Lionel? One last time?'."

articles.title: Esta Roma es la Lecce
articles.standfirst: Otro recital de 'La Loba' para seguir como el mejor equipo de este arranque de Serie A
articles.summary: Otro recital de 'La Loba' para seguir como el mejor equipo de este arranque de Serie A
articles.body: La Roma de Gasperini se confirmó en el Via del Mare de Lecce como el equipo más solvente de este arranque de Serie A 2026-27. Si en el debut ganó 4-0 a la Fiorentina en el Olímpico, ahora se impuso 0-4 a domicilio al equipo del sur de Italia que entrena un ex como Eusebio Di Francesco. El partido duró 25 minutos. Fue lo que tardó Malen en destrozar a la zaga 'leccesi'. El neerlandés, que ya hizo 'hat-trick' a la Fiore, firmó un doblete para encarrilar el duelo. El ex del Aston Villa, comprado por 25 millones este verano tras su cesión inicial en enero, ha marcado 19 goles en sus primeros 20 partidos en Serie A. En la historia del torneo, solo Gunnar Nordahl (20 goles, en 1949) y José Altafini (20, entre 1958 y 1959) lo han superado en la misma cantidad de partidos. Histórico. El propio Malen, que tuvo varias ocasiones más para desatar una auténtica goleada en el primer tiempo, originó el 0-3... de Matías Soulé. La Roma era un vendaval imposible de frenar para un Lecce que, si bien había ganado en la primera jornada al Venezia, peleará por no descender otra temporada más. Redondeó la goleada, ya en la segunda parte, un Rodrigo Mora que sigue deslumbrando en la capital italiana. Fue titular ante la Fiorentina, con un buen estreno, y entrando desde el banquillo en Lecce firmó su primer tanto como 'giallorosso'.

articles.title: La Selección femenina se prueba para la Main Round de la Eurocopa
articles.standfirst: Catorce elegidas por Clàudia Pons para el doble amistoso ante Polonia (Las Rozas, 8 y 9 de septiembre)
articles.summary: Catorce elegidas por Clàudia Pons para el doble amistoso ante Polonia (Las Rozas, 8 y 9 de septiembre)
articles.body: la Selección femenina, que dirige Clàudia Pons, retomará la actividad los próximos martes y miércoles, 8 y 9 de septiembre, con dos amistosos ante Polonia, que se jugarán en el Pabellón La Marazuela (20:00 el martes y 18:30 el miércoles) uno de los rivales de la selección en la fase de clasificación para el Mundial de Filipinas disputada en Besançon el año pasado. Para este partido, Clàudia Pons contará con la base de las jugadoras que afrontarán la fase de clasificación para el Europeo de 2027 en Eslovenia, que ejercerá de anfitriona de esta Elite Round en la que España se medirá a Francia (7 de octubre, 16:30), Italia (8 de octubre, 16:30) y Eslovenia (10 de octubre, 17:30) en busca de una de las plazas para la Eurocopa que se jugará en Osijek (Croacia), del 14 al 21 de marzo de 2026. Las convocadas son: Ari (Arriva AD Alcorcón) y Elena (Poio Pescamar), como porteras; Mayte Mateo y Cecilia (STV Roldán) y Martita (Poio Pescamar), como cierres; Ale de Paz (Poio Pescamar) y Antía Pérez (Bloques Cando Castro) como ala-cierres. Para el ala: Irene Samper (Melilla Ciudad del Deporte Torreblanca), Eva (STV Roldán), Clau López (Arriva AD Alcorcón) y María Sanz (Atlético Navalcarnero); Laura Sánchez (Poio Pescamar); ala-pívot y Vane Sotelo (Arriva AD Alcorcón) e Irene Córdoba (Atlético Navalcarnero), pívots. Por cierto, los partidos de la Primera Iberdrola, que comienza el viernes con el Estrela Revoltosa Verín FSF - FSF Castro Bloques Cando (21:00), y que no sean retransmitidos por Teledeporte o RTVE Play, se podrán ver en el canal de You Tube de la Federación Española de Fútbol.

articles.title: Deivid Washington, el preferido para completar la delantera del Sevilla
articles.standfirst: Los hispalenses negocian la cesión del futbolista del Chelsea y pregunta condiciones al Saint-Étienne por Lucas Stassin
articles.summary: Los hispalenses negocian la cesión del futbolista del Chelsea y pregunta condiciones al Saint-Étienne por Lucas Stassin
articles.body: Después de caerse las opciones de George Ilenikhena, Conrad Harder y Petar Ratkov, el Sevilla ha intensificado los contactos para incorporar a Deivid Washington, delantero de 21 años perteneciente al Chelsea y que también puede jugar como extremo. La dirección deportiva quiere cerrar su llegada a préstamo, una posibilidad que trascendió hace algunas semanas y que ahora pasa a primer plano. El futbolista brasileño, busca los minutos que no le ofrecen en el conjunto blue, donde su participación ha sido prácticamente inexistente. En el Sevilla ven en Deivid Washington la pieza idónea para complementar a Robbie Ure e Isaac Romero. Sin embargo, no es la única opción que se maneja en el club. Según informa el periodista Sacha Tavolieri, los nervionenses también han preguntado por la situación de Lucas Stassin. El delantero belga del Saint-Étienne, que ya sonó en el pasado verano para reforzar el ataque, llegaría cedido con opción de compra, una operación que se negocia en paralelo con la del jugador del Chelsea. Al margen de lo que suceda con Rubén Vargas, cuya venta al Olympiacos se ha frenado por desavenencias económicas sevillistas, el Sevilla tiene intención de fichar al menos un extremo que ocupe la vacante que ha dejado Oso. En este sentido, L'Équipe apunta como serio candidato a Félix Correia. Según informa el diario francés, la entidad hispalense ya negocia con el Lille otra cesión con opción de compra. El extremo portugués de 25 años, fichado por el conjunto galo por 7 millones de euros tras destacar en el Gil Vicente, vería con muy buenos ojos aterrizar en el fútbol español.

articles.title: Derek McInnes: Rangers manager's touchline ban changed after appeal over 'disgusting' comment last season
articles.summary: Rangers appealed the four-match ban handed to Derek McInnes; former Hearts boss described the awarding of a penalty to Celtic at Motherwell as "disgusting"; McInnes will now serve an immediate two-match touchline ban instead of three after appeal hearing
articles.body:
The 55-year-old was initially handed a four-match suspension by the Scottish FA, with three of those games to be served immediately.

While the overall ban remains in place, he will now only serve two of those with immediate effect, while the other two will only be triggered should he breach disciplinary rule 72 again before the end of this season.

It's after the former Hearts boss described the penalty awarded to Celtic against Motherwell's last May as "disgusting".

The first game McInnes will be in the stands for is Wednesday's trip to Falkirk, live on Sky Sports, followed by their game at Ibrox against Motherwell on Saturday.

It means McInnes will return to the touchline for their league match against St Mirren next Wednesday.

Following that is their Old Firm double-header as Celtic visit in the League Cup on September 13, before a trip to Celtic Park in the Premiership a week later - live on Sky Sports.

McInnes has endured a tough start to life as Rangers manager, with his side knocked out of Europe completely after Europa League and then Conference League defeats.

Domestically, Sunday's win at Aberdeen was his first in the Premiership , with the club five points behind Celtic after three games.

In May, then Hearts head coach McInnes saw his side beat Falkirk in their penultimate league match. Meanwhile, Celtic were being held at Motherwell, meaning Hearts were set to go three points clear at the top and had a better goal difference over Celtic. That meant Hearts would be crowned champions if they avoided a heavy defeat at Parkhead on the final day.

However, in added time, Celtic were awarded a late penalty at Fir Park following a VAR check for a handball by Motherwell's Sam Nicholson . That was converted to seal victory for Martin O'Neill's side, and leave the gap between the sides at just one point.

McInnes said the decision to issue the spot-kick was "disgusting". Celtic then went on to beat Hearts on the final day, denying them a first top-flight title in 66 years .

Former Motherwell player Elliot Watt was handed a four-match ban by the SFA for describing that penalty award as the "worst VAR decision in history".

The Fir Park side were also fined £5,000 after their own social media post following that match.

articles.title: Enzo Fernandez transfer news: Man City open talks with Chelsea to sign Argentina midfielder
articles.summary: Enzo Fernandez joined Chelsea from Benfica for £107m in 2023; the Argentine played in Chelsea's first Premier League game of the season against Fulham but was not involved against Luton in the Carabao Cup and left out again when they faced Brighton
articles.body:
Sky Sports News reported that Chelsea were prepared to sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for the right price - and if they can improve their squad before the window closes.

Man City's interest in Fernandez remains despite missing Chelsea's August 14 deadline to bid for him.

Chelsea had agreed with Fernandez's representatives that he could be sold for £120m by that deadline, but an offer never arrived.

Reinforcing central midfield has become an even bigger priority for City following Rodri's departure to Barcelona earlier this month.

Nico Gonzalez has also left to join Newcastle in a transfer worth up to £50m, with Tijjani Reijnders recently departing for Al Qadsiah for £51m. Bernardo Silva left City following the expiry of his contract and has since joined Real Madrid.

City have completed the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille with the midfielder moving to the Etihad Stadium for £86m in a world-record deal for a teenager.

articles.title: “The best decisions aren’t made with your mind, but with your instinct”: Lionel Messi’s career, legacy and final lesson in trusting yourself
articles.summary: International Sports News: For Lionel Messi, football was never only about making the safest choice. His career was built on moments when he trusted what he felt, even when the .
articles.body: For Lionel Messi, football was never only about making the safest choice. His career was built on moments when he trusted what he felt, even when the decision in front of him was difficult. From leaving Argentina as a young boy to chasing his dream in Barcelona, from returning to the national team after walking away in 2016 to finally lifting the World Cup in 2022, Messi repeatedly followed his instinct. Now, as he steps away from international football at 39, his famous words: “The best decisions aren’t made with your mind, but with your instinct” feel even more meaningful.What does Lionel Messi’s quote about instinct really mean?Messi’s words are not about ignoring logic. They are about knowing yourself well enough to trust what feels right. In football, he often had only seconds to decide whether to pass, shoot or take on a defender. His greatest moments came from trusting that instinct instead of overthinking.The same idea can be seen in his life away from the pitch. Messi has faced choices that could have changed his entire career. Instead of always choosing what looked easiest, he followed the path that felt right to him.That is what makes the quote so powerful. Sometimes, the mind sees fear, doubt and risk. Instinct sees what you truly want.How did Messi follow his instinct when his biggest dreams seemed far away?Messi’s journey was never simple. As a young player from Rosario, Argentina, he moved to Spain to join Barcelona’s youth system and began building a career that would eventually make him one of football’s greatest players. But his Argentina journey was much harder.Messi reached major finals with Argentina and suffered painful defeats. Argentina lost the 2014 World Cup final to Germany and then lost the 2015 and 2016 Copa América finals to Chile. After the 2016 Copa América final, Messi briefly announced his international retirement.Yet he came back. That decision changed everything. Messi trusted that his story with Argentina was not finished. He eventually won the 2021 Copa América, the 2022 World Cup and the 2024 Copa América.His return showed that instinct can sometimes tell you to keep going when disappointment tells you to stop.How did Messi turn years of heartbreak into a legacy?Messi’s legacy was not created by avoiding failure. It was created by refusing to let failure make the final decision for him.For years, he was compared with Argentina’s greatest football icons and was questioned because he had not won a major senior international trophy. The pressure became especially heavy after the defeats in 2014, 2015 and 2016.But Messi kept returning to the same dream.When he finally lifted the Copa América trophy in 2021, Argentina’s long wait for a major title was over. A year later, he reached the top of international football by leading Argentina to the 2022 World Cup title in Qatar.That journey gave a deeper meaning to his quote. Trusting yourself does not mean you will always make the right decision immediately. Sometimes, it means believing in yourself long enough to discover where that decision can take you.What does Messi’s retirement teach us about knowing when to let go?On August 31, 2026, Messi announced his retirement from international football after Argentina reached the 2026 World Cup final and lost to Spain. It brought an end to a 21-year Argentina career in which he became the team’s most-capped player and leading goalscorer.There was no perfect ending. Messi had already experienced the joy of winning the World Cup, but he could not finish his international career with another title.And perhaps that is another lesson hidden inside his words.Trusting your instinct is not always about knowing when to fight. Sometimes, it is also about knowing when your journey has reached the point where it is time to step away.Messi leaves Argentina with a legacy built on much more than trophies. He leaves behind the story of a player who endured criticism, heartbreak, disappointment and impossible expectations, yet kept choosing the game he loved.His career shows that the biggest decisions in life are not always the ones that look perfect on paper. Sometimes, you simply have to trust yourself, take the chance and keep walking. Messi did that for more than two decades. And that may be the most inspiring part of his legacy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Brizuela muy crítico: "El arbitraje ha sido malo con alevosía"
articles.standfirst: El del Barcelona y Aday Mara hablaron del partido y de las decisiones arbitrales
articles.summary: El del Barcelona y Aday Mara hablaron del partido y de las decisiones arbitrales
articles.body: Darío Brizuela salió contrariado a hablar del partido. Hizo un tremendo esfuerzo en la prórroga para meter a España de lleno con ocho puntos seguidos, y el azulgrana mostraba la frustración por la derrota y por cómo se había producido. "Jode perder siempre, sea cual sea la circunstancia, pero hoy especialmente después de habernos esforzado tanto". Brizuela elevó mucho más la voz cuando habló del arbitraje del partido: "Sabíamos dónde estábamos y el arbitraje ha sido malo con alevosía y esto es la FIBA, lo tienen que mirar. El trío arbitral que venga tiene que tener la profesionalidad de poder arbitrar en el OAKA. Luego les preguntabas por las acciones y no sabían ni qué responderte". Sobre la jugada de la eliminación de Mara, Brizuela lo tiene claro: "Se ve claramente en el videomarcador que Aday no le toca la cara, sino el hombro. Pero se revisa y se pita antideportiva, luego en otra más clara como antideportiva (se refiere a la última con Parra), no se revisa porque si la van a revisar la tienen que pitar antideportiva. Jode, pero es el contexto en el que se juega y ni es culpa nuestra ni es culpa de Grecia y quien lo tiene que mirar es la FIBA". Al final, el español aprovechó para añadir: "Tengo que decir que no nos han dejado firmar el acta y me gustaría saber exactamente por qué. Nos han dicho que íbamos tarde, pero cuánto tiempo tenemos si un partido acaba y los árbitros se van corriendo". Sobre lo que queda y el reto que España tiene por delante, Darío dijo: "Es obvio que este verano no hemos tenido los resultados que queríamos. No hemos estado bien ni en esta Ventana ni en la anterior y eso es malo porque no sólo veníamos ganando sino también jugando muy bien. El plan de Chus se veía perfectamente por dónde iba y obviamente la responsabilidad de las derrotas es de los que hemos estado aquí". Aday Mara también estuvo a un excelente nivel hasta que los árbitros decidieron sacarle del partido. Analizó así el choque ante Grecia: "Comparándolo con el de Zaragoza, he visto una mejoría en ganas, en creer y en ir a ganar el partido. El plan antes del partido era un buen plan pero esa falta de experiencia nos ha fallado en algún momento", y luego se mostró irónico: "Y creo que en los últimos minutos los árbitros han hecho un gran trabajo, sobre todo porque sus ataques eran todo tiros libres, lo que no es mal plan de partido porque no se pueden defender unos tiros libres y así es complicado parar al equipo rival. También hubo varias eliminaciones que creo que habría que mirar un poco cómo han sido. Y la última jugada me ha parecido bien pitada porque en ningún sitio de las reglas FIBA pone que a falta de esos minutos y con ese tipo de faltas hay que ir a revisarlas y lo han hecho fenomenal (risas). Pero tampoco tiene que servir de excusa porque hay muchas cosas que mejorar".

articles.title: Texas' Steve Sarkisian Explains Why Adding Former NFL Players Is Morally 'Wrong' amid LSU Criticism
articles.summary: It seems like Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian will not be adding any players to the Longhorns roster who previously reached the professional level.
articles.body:
It seems like Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian will not be adding any players to the Longhorns roster who previously reached the professional level.

"The fact that somebody out there is going to take a player off of an NFL roster and tell somebody who's been doing it for nine months to go kick rocks, that doesn't sit well with me," Sarkisian told reporters Monday. "I think that's wrong. That, morally, is wrong."

His comments come amid controversy regarding fellow SEC school LSU.

Lane Kiffin and the Tigers have aimed to add players such as tight end Dae'Quan Wright, defensive lineman Zxavian Harrison and edge-rusher Junior Tuihalamaka, but the SEC issued a statement saying it planned on preventing athletes from returning to the college ranks after they were on pro teams:

However, a Texas judge issued an order overruling the conference's statement.

Kiffin told ESPN's Pete Thamel he is in "daily communication" with the SEC regarding the issue and clarified the rule "does not prohibit players from practicing at the school, it prohibits them from being added to the final 105 roster, which has to be turned in on Friday."

LSU opens its 2026 season on Saturday in a highly anticipated showdown against Clemson.

The Tigers also play Sarkisian and the Longhorns this season on Nov. 14, and the comments and separate approaches to the issue figure to remain a storyline in the lead up to that contest.
